Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Peritonsillar abscess (PTA) after surgical tonsil removal is an infrequent complication. Residual lymphoid tissue after tonsillotomy may increase this risk compared to tonsillectomy. This study aimed to identify cases of PTA following tonsillotomy or tonsillectomy in a pediatric population and compare the incidence and case details. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective comparative case series. SETTING: Tertiary pediatric hospital. METHODS: A review was conducted of patients ≤18 years of age who underwent tonsillotomy or tonsillectomy from January 2010 to January 2025 and later presented with PTA. Among 5576 tonsillotomies and 19,834 tonsillectomies performed, 10 patients were identified in whom PTA occurred after tonsil surgery at the study institution, and for whom complete medical records were available. RESULTS: Nine cases of PTA occurred after tonsillotomy (0.16%) and one after tonsillectomy (0.005%). The mean interval (±SD) from tonsil surgery to PTA diagnosis was 8.2 ± 3.0 years (range, 1-12 years). Mean age at PTA diagnosis was 13.7 ± 2.3 years (range, 10-18 years). Residual tonsillar tissue was confirmed in seven of ten patients; five underwent revision tonsillectomy. CONCLUSION: The benefits of tonsillotomy over tonsillectomy with respect to short-term postoperative morbidity are well established. Although the long-term risk of PTA secondary to residual lymphoid tissue is low, otolaryngologists should be aware of this possible outcome when counseling patients preoperatively as to intracapsular tonsillotomy versus extracapsular tonsillectomy, and when treating patients with pharyngeal symptoms with a history of prior intracapsular tonsillotomy. item.title: Immune Profiles and Immunotherapy Efficacy in Sinonasal Malignancies: A Scoping Review.
item.dc:creator: Ali A, Hamdan A, Shah A, Alvi A, Issa E, Haleem A, Cantrell S, Thorpe R, Jang DW, Goldstein BJ, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Ali A, Hamdan A, Shah A, Alvi A, Issa E, Haleem A, Cantrell S, Thorpe R, Jang DW, Goldstein BJ, et al.
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70411
Published: 2026-Oct-17
PMID: 42891574



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Little is understood about the efficacy of immunotherapeutic strategies against sinonasal malignancies (SN) or their immunologic profiles. This review summarizes key immune markers within SN tumors and underscores known data on the efficacy of checkpoint inhibitors. DATA SOURCES: The MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science databases were searched from database inception to present to identify studies on SN malignancies, including SN squamous cell carcinoma (SNSCCa), adenocarcinoma (SNAC), undifferentiated carcinoma (SNUC), and olfactory neuroblastoma (ONB), their immune profiles, and immunotherapy efficacy. REVIEW METHODS: Included studies were those that either investigated the tumor immune profile (cellular or molecular) or reported findings following the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Two separate teams of two reviewers performed dual, independent screening and full-text review of 675 studies, with 52 included in the final analysis. RESULTS: Anti-programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1) immunotherapy is the most investigated immune checkpoint inhibitor against SN malignancies. Checkpoint inhibitor efficacy showed the most promise for SNSCCa with comparatively few studies in SNAC, SNUC, and ONB. The prognostic value of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL) density and programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) expression vary greatly between SN tumor subtypes. TILs, not PD-L1 expression, most consistently correlate with survival in SNSCCa, SNAC, and SNUC. ONBs are predominantly immune-cold. CONCLUSION: SN tumor rarity and heterogeneity limits research in immunotherapy efficacy and prognostic biomarkers. Multi-institutional research endeavors aimed at evaluating both checkpoint inhibitor efficacy and the SN tumor immune microenvironment are essential in advancing SN tumor management.

item.title: Cannabis Use and Prolonged Opioid Utilization After Head and Neck Free Flap Reconstructive Surgery.
item.dc:creator: Jackert EP, Gallagher T, Gamero M, Thompson Z, Li A, Kokot NC
item.description:
Authors: Jackert EP, Gallagher T, Gamero M, Thompson Z, Li A, Kokot NC
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71002
Published: 2026-Oct-16
PMID: 42888518



Abstract:
GOAL: This study investigates the risk of prolonged postoperative opioid use and functional outcomes of free flap reconstruction in head and neck cancer patients with a history of cannabis use. METHODS: Patients undergoing head and neck free flap reconstruction (2005-2025) were identified using the TriNetX database and stratified by cannabis use. Cohorts were propensity score-matched for demographics, substance use, and tumor characteristics. The primary outcome was postoperative opioid use at 3-12 months; secondary outcomes included tracheostomy and gastrostomy dependence. Multivariable Cox regression adjusted for behavioral health comorbidities. RESULTS: After matching, each cohort (cannabis users and non-users) consisted of 532 patients. Cannabis users were more likely to be gastrostomy tube dependent at 3 months (RR: 1.56, 95% CI: [1.19-2.04]). Preoperative cannabis use increased the risk of prolonged postoperative opioid use at 3-6 months (RR: 1.19, 95% CI: [1.05-1.36]), 6-9 months (RR: 1.35, 95% CI: [1.13-1.62]), and 9-12 months (RR: 1.26, 95% CI: [1.04-1.52]). There was no significant difference in tracheostomy dependence at any time point. In adjusted Cox regression analysis, perioperative cannabis persisted as independently associated with prolonged opioid use (HR: 1.42, 90% CI: [1.14, 1.76]). CONCLUSION: Head and neck cancer patients with a history of cannabis use demonstrate increased risk of prolonged opioid use after free flap reconstructive surgery even after adjusting for behavioral health comorbidities, highlighting the need for targeted pain management strategies and closer postoperative monitoring in this patient population.

item.title: Waiting times and determinants of delay for head and neck cancer in England-a population cohort study using real world data.
item.dc:creator: Jashek-Ahmed F, Almilaji O, Cowling TE, Hamilton DW, Walker K, Paleri V
item.description:
Authors: Jashek-Ahmed F, Almilaji O, Cowling TE, Hamilton DW, Walker K, Paleri V
Journal: British journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1038/s41416-026-03630-8
Published: 2026-Oct-16
PMID: 42888204



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Head and Neck Cancer (HNC), even short delays in treatment can worsen prognosis. We used real-world data to quantify waiting times and identify patient, tumour and health service factors associated with treatment delay in England. METHODS: Using linked national datasets (Cancer Registry, Cancer Waiting Times, Hospital Episodes Statistics, Radiotherapy and Chemotherapy), we calculated waiting times from referral to first treatment (surgery or (chemo)radiation) and used multivariable logistic regression models to examine factors associated with delay. RESULTS: Of 30,506 patients, 43% experienced treatment delay ( > 62 days from referral). Long delays ( > 90 days) affected 11% of patients treated with primary surgery and 20% of those receiving primary (chemo)radiation. Non-urgent referral (30% of patients) was the strongest predictor of long delay (aOR 4.07, CI: 3.54-4.68). Additional risk-factors included initial assessment at non-specialist (spoke) hospitals, non-oropharyngeal cancers, and higher socio-economic deprivation. CONCLUSIONS: Treatment delays in HNC are worsening, particularly for patients treated with primary (chemo)radiation. Referral route is the strongest determinant. Interventions should focus on optimising referral pathways, increasing awareness of HNC symptoms among the public and primary care, and acknowledging the different drivers of delay associated with surgery and (chemo)radiation therapy.

item.title: US-based Delphi Consensus Study on Adjuvant Radiation Therapy (ART) in Node-Negative Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma (CSCC).
item.dc:creator: Stevens JS, Barker CA, Bakst RL, Bradford C, Carr DR, Chera B, Chen M, Chandra S, Demer A, Donnelly H, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Stevens JS, Barker CA, Bakst RL, Bradford C, Carr DR, Chera B, Chen M, Chandra S, Demer A, Donnelly H, et al.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics | DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrobp.2026.09.022
Published: 2026-Oct-16
PMID: 42887677



Abstract:
PURPOSE: There is a paucity of high-level evidence for adjuvant radiation therapy (ART) in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) creating practice variations. This study provides expert consensus recommendations on patient and tumor selection, timing, duration, dosage, and additional considerations for ART in node-negative CSCC. METHODS: The Delphi panel included 35 experts in radiation oncology (15), dermatology/Mohs micrographic surgery (9), medical oncology (7), head and neck surgery (3), and surgical oncology (1). Consensus was defined as ≥80% concordance; near-consensus 70-79% concordance. RESULTS: Consensus was reached to recommend ART when further surgery is not possible, but the tumor has positive gross or histologic/microscopic margins (35/35, 100%). Key consensus or near-consensus recommendations for recommending ART to the tumor bed following negative-margin surgery include: 5-year cumulative incidence of local recurrence (29/35, 83%) or nodal metastasis (27/35, 77%) ≥ 20%; gross cortical bone/marrow invasion (32/35, 91%); skull base invasion (32/35, 91%); 4 risk factors (RF) (35/35, 100%); 3 RF (30-33/35, 86-94%); PNI ≥ 0.1 mm and one other RF (30/35, 86%); and clinical nerve invasion (31/35, 89%). Immune status influenced ART decision-making (30/35, 86%) with 77% (27/35) more likely to recommend ART for immunosuppressed patients. Consensus was reached to omit ART for pathologic complete response following neoadjuvant immunotherapy (34/35, 97%). Among radiation oncologists, 100% (15/15) agreed the optimal window for ART to the tumor bed is 4-8 weeks and that hypofractionated regimens can be appropriate (12/15, 80%). Consensus was reached for prescription doses of 60-66 Gy in 2 Gy/fx (15/15, 100%) or 50-55 Gy in 2.5 Gy/fx (13/15, 87%), and that superficial radiation and brachytherapy are inappropriate ART modalities for node-negative high-stage CSCC (14/15, 93%). There was no consensus on elective nodal basin irradiation. CONCLUSIONS: This Delphi study provides an expert consensus-based framework to standardize ART for node-negative high-stage CSCC following surgery, informing future guidelines and utilization.

item.title: Firmonertinib in advanced non-small cell lung cancer with epidermal growth factor receptor P-loop and αC-helix compressing mutations.
item.dc:creator: Le X, Wang J, Yu Y, Zhao Y, Planchard D, Gao B, Spira A, Liu J, Li X, Gadgeel S, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Le X, Wang J, Yu Y, Zhao Y, Planchard D, Gao B, Spira A, Liu J, Li X, Gadgeel S, et al.
Journal: Cancer cell | DOI: 10.1016/j.ccell.2026.09.011
Published: 2026-Oct-16
PMID: 42887497



Abstract:
P-loop and αC-helix compressing (PACC) mutations comprise a structurally distinct subgroup of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with limited treatment options. Firmonertinib is a once-daily oral, brain-penetrant, mutant-selective EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor with a unique trifluoroethoxy side chain. Firmonertinib had high anti-proliferative efficacy in EGFR PACC-mutant cells and xenografts. In the phase 1b FURTHER study (NCT05364073), patients with metastatic EGFR PACC-mutant NSCLC randomized to receive first-line firmonertinib 160 mg (n = 25) or 240 mg (n = 22) had confirmed objective response rates (ORRs) of 43% and 68%, median duration of response not reached and 14.6 months, and median progression-free survival of 11.1 and 16.0 months, respectively; treatment-related adverse events led to dose reductions (19% and 24%) and discontinuation (3% and 0%). Intracranial ORR among patients with brain metastases at baseline was 47% (8/17). Results support further study of first-line firmonertinib in patients with EGFR PACC-mutant NSCLC.

item.title: Oncological and quality-of-life outcomes after robotic versus open neck dissection in oral cavity cancer: a prospective matched-pair analysis.
item.dc:creator: Gupta K, Popat S, Sarin D
item.description:
Authors: Gupta K, Popat S, Sarin D
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108185
Published: 2026-Oct-16
PMID: 42887359



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neck dissection remains the standard of care for regional control of nodal disease in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma, but the conventional trans-cervical approach leaves a visible scar and carries a recognized risk of shoulder morbidity. Remote-access robotic neck dissection has been proposed as a means of preserving oncological adequacy while improving cosmetic and functional outcomes. We report a prospective matched-pair comparison of retro-auricular robotic neck dissection and standard open neck dissection in patients with oral cavity cancer. METHODS: Sixty-four patients undergoing neck dissection for oral cavity carcinoma between January 2020 and December 2025 were enrolled and matched 1:1 by age, sex, tumour subsite and clinical stage; 32 underwent retro-auricular robotic neck dissection and 32 underwent conventional open neck dissection. Oncological adequacy was assessed by lymph node yield per dissection; quality of life and shoulder function were measured with the Neck Dissection Impairment Index (NDII); and cosmetic outcome was assessed with a structured patient-reported questionnaire. RESULTS: Mean lymph node yield was comparable between the robotic and open groups (23.9 vs 24.6 nodes per dissection; p = 0.542). Mean NDII scores at 3 weeks were similar (65.7 vs 64.2; p = 0.261) and improved over time in both groups. Patient-reported cosmetic satisfaction was significantly higher after robotic neck dissection (12.3 vs 8.0; p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Retro-auricular robotic neck dissection achieves an oncological yield, quality-of-life and shoulder function outcome equivalent to open neck dissection, with a markedly superior cosmetic result, and merits consideration in appropriately selected patients with oral cavity cancer.

item.title: Quantifying the diagnostic time gap in precision oncology: A retrospective analysis of potential time savings from same-day cartridge-based molecular testing versus next-generation sequencing in cytology specimens.
item.dc:creator: Tran K, Chen E, Symmans WF, Sura GH
item.description:
Authors: Tran K, Chen E, Symmans WF, Sura GH
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360239
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42886752



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) turnaround times (TAT) exceed two weeks and can delay the initiation of targeted therapy. Rapid cartridge-based platforms such as Idylla deliver single-gene or fusion results from minimal cytology material within hours, but time savings have not been systematically quantified. METHODS: Forty-two cases of non-small cell lung carcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, melanoma, and mammary analogue secretory carcinoma of the salivary gland that underwent both Idylla testing (KRAS, EGFR, BRAF, and GeneFusion assays) and orthogonal NGS at a single academic center were reviewed. NGS TAT was calculated from specimen collection to report release, and Idylla results were modeled as available one day after collection. The primary outcome was per-case time savings (NGS TAT minus one day); treatment timelines were reconstructed from the medical record. Analyses were descriptive; no inferential testing was performed. A sensitivity analysis varied the modeled Idylla TAT from 1 to 3 days, and an adjusted estimate assigned no time saving to the two cartridge results that were not actionable on the day of collection. RESULTS: The median NGS TAT across all 42 cases was 20.0 days (IQR, 17.0-23.8; range, 8-51). Against the modeled 1-day Idylla TAT, the median time savings was 19.0 days per case (IQR, 16.0-22.8; range, 7-50), totaling 858 patient-days. Assigning no time saving to those two cases gave a median of 18.0 days and 817 patient-days. No patient received therapy that was subsequently contradicted by the sequencing result. In thirteen patients, the sequencing interval alone exceeded three weeks, and in seven, no systemic therapy was underway while the result was awaited. CONCLUSIONS: Same-day cartridge-based testing from cytology and small biopsy specimens could provide actionable results a median of 19 days earlier than standard NGS. Whether this translates into earlier treatment initiation was not assessed and requires prospective evaluation.

item.title: The relationship between the use of fillers and Japanese proficiency: Focusing on OPI level assessment.
item.dc:creator: Chen Z
item.description:
Authors: Chen Z
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360747
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42886675



Abstract:
This study employed a Cumulative Link Mixed Model (CLMM) to examine the relationship between Japanese learners' filler use and OPI (Oral Proficiency Interview) level ratings. The results showed no significant association with proficiency for the i(い)-group, u(う)-group, ano(あの)-group, and eeto(ええと)-group fillers. In contrast, the a(あ)-group, e(え)-group, o(お)-group, and n(ん)-group fillers were significantly negatively associated with higher proficiency, while the use of maa(まあ)-group and sono(その)-group fillers was significantly positively associated with higher proficiency. Furthermore, an analysis of maa(まあ)-group and sono(その)-group fillers based on their functions and discourse roles showed that turn-internal maa(まあ) and inferential/re-presenting sono(その) require at least two clauses to be produced. This indicates a connection with paragraph-level language production, which is one of the criteria for 'Text Type' in OPI assessment. It was also found that the use of these fillers with such functions is significantly positively associated with higher proficiency. On the other hand, for fillers such as ano(あの) and eeto(ええと), as well as maa(まあ) used in adjacency pairs, no significant increase with proficiency was observed, confirming that their use is not associated with paragraph-level production. The use of fillers linked to paragraph-level production can be considered one of the key linguistic factors that can help explain the relationship between filler use and the development of oral language proficiency.

item.title: Molecular screening of selected RNA viruses in neotropical wild felids of Brazil.
item.dc:creator: Colpani M, Duarte-Benvenuto A, Sacristán C, Bueno MG, de Moraes MTB, Zamana-Ramblas R, Codeas BS, Navas-Suarez PE, Arias-Lugo MA, Morato RG, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Colpani M, Duarte-Benvenuto A, Sacristán C, Bueno MG, de Moraes MTB, Zamana-Ramblas R, Codeas BS, Navas-Suarez PE, Arias-Lugo MA, Morato RG, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0359169
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42886669



Abstract:
Astrovirus, cardiovirus and rotavirus are RNA viruses widely distributed among humans, domestic and wild mammals, including felids, occasionally associated with fatal outbreaks and highly resistant to environmental conditions. Despite this, there are no reports of these viruses in New World felids. The aim of this study was to investigate the presence of astrovirus, rotavirus and cardiovirus in non-domestic felids under human care or in the wild, across multiple Brazilian biomes (i.e., Amazon Forest, Atlantic Forest, Caatinga, and Cerrado). Biological samples (e.g., blood, oral and rectal swabs, and frozen tissues) were submitted to reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) for astrovirus detection and real-time RT-PCR for rotavirus and cardiovirus, followed by sequencing. Fifty wild felids were analyzed, comprising 40 free-ranging and 10 captive animals: 19 ocelots (Leopardus pardalis), 12 pumas (Puma concolor), seven jaguarundis (Herpailurus yagouaroundi), six southern tiger cats (Leopardus guttulus), three margays (Leopardus wiedii) and three jaguars (Panthera onca). An astrovirus was detected in rectal swab of a healthy captive southern tiger cat, while a genotype G3P[3] Rotavirus alphagastroenteritidis (Rotavirus A) was detected in intestine of a roadkill puma. All felid samples were negative for cardiovirus. Morphological analyses of available formalin-fixed tissues of the rotavirus-positive puma were inconclusive due to autolysis. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first molecular detection of astrovirus and rotavirus in Neotropical wild felid species.

item.title: Concurrent TMS-EEG to characterise interhemispheric signal propagation over the motor and prefrontal regions: An independent replication of GABAB receptor mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: Zhou J, He Y, Jin C, Yang C, Han Y, Wang Y, Zhen Z, Huang Z, Shi S, Che X, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zhou J, He Y, Jin C, Yang C, Han Y, Wang Y, Zhen Z, Huang Z, Shi S, Che X, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360250
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42886653



Abstract:
Callosal abnormalities disrupt interhemispheric communications that impair the recovery of a series of neurological and psychiatric disorders. Understanding interhemispheric communication could help identify treatments for disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission. This study aimed to validate the sensitivity of a TMS-EEG-based measure of interhemispheric signal propagation (ISP) to GABAB receptor modulation, while independently replicating the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition. A group of 29 participants received an oral dose of either baclofen, a GABAB receptor agonist, or a placebo. Before and after drug intake, single-pulse TMS-EEG was applied to assess ISP in both the motor and prefrontal regions. Our findings indicated that baclofen increased interhemispheric inhibition over the motor region, indexed by significantly decreased ISP (p = 0.037). No significant effect was observed in the dorsolateral prefrontal region (p = 0.186), suggesting regional specificity in GABAB receptor modulation of ISP. These findings uncovered the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition as indexed by ISP. They also highlight the potential of ISP for characterising interhemispheric communication, which could inform the treatment for a series of disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission.

item.title: Multidimensional oral health and frailty in older adults: A sex-stratified cross-sectional study.
item.dc:creator: Yang JE, Moon S
item.description:
Authors: Yang JE, Moon S
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360682
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42886645



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty in older adults is a critical public health concern associated with increased morbidity, disability, and healthcare utilization. Although systemic health and socioeconomic factors are well-established determinants of frailty, the multidimensional nature of oral health has received relatively limited attention in previous research. The aim of this study was to examine the associations between general characteristics, health-related factors, oral health factors, and frailty among community-dwelling older adults, and to identify sex differences in frailty. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from the 2022 Korean Longitudinal Study of Aging (KLoSA) and included 3,729 individuals aged 65 years and older. Frailty was categorized as robust, pre-frail, or frail using the Frailty Instrument developed for older Korean adults. General characteristics, health-related factors, and oral health-related factors (structural, behavioral, and subjective) were assessed through structured questionnaires. Hierarchical logistic regression analysis was performed in three steps to identify factors associated with frailty. RESULTS: Of the participants, 16.0% were frail and 84.0% were non-frail (31.5% pre-frail and 52.5% robust). Sex-stratified analyses also showed that structural oral health factors were most strongly associated with frailty in both sexes. Edentulous status without denture use was associated with the highest odds of frailty in both women (OR = 3.76, 95% CI = 3.72-3.80) and men (OR = 2.95, 95% CI = 2.91-2.98). In contrast, sex differences were observed for some subjective oral health factors: tooth sensitivity was associated with higher odds of frailty in women (OR = 1.82, 95% CI = 1.80-1.84) but lower odds in men (OR = 0.85, 95% CI = 0.84-0.86). CONCLUSIONS: Oral health conditions, including untreated tooth loss, difficulty in chewing or swallowing, and oral pain, were significantly associated with frailty. These findings suggest that oral health may be an important factor to consider in relation to frailty among community-dwelling older adults.

item.title: Cutaneous Leiomyosarcoma of the Head and Neck: Appreciation of a More Indolent Biological Behavior and Implications for Its Management.
item.dc:creator: de Bree E, de Bree R, Chiesa-Estomba C, Guntinas-Lichius O, Sreeram MP, Michelakis D, Rao KN, Rinaldo A, Ferlito A
item.description:
Authors: de Bree E, de Bree R, Chiesa-Estomba C, Guntinas-Lichius O, Sreeram MP, Michelakis D, Rao KN, Rinaldo A, Ferlito A
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70512
Published: 2026-Oct-15
PMID: 42885217



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leiomysosarcoma (LMS) is generally associated with high metastatic potential and poor survival. Cutaneous LMS (cLMS) has been considered a different entity with more indolent biological behavior. METHODS: A narrative review was performed to assess the biological behavior of cLMS, with special attention for the head and neck location. RESULTS: cLMS is located in the head and neck in 21%-33%. The local recurrence rate is 2%-18%, while only 3% develops metastatic disease at 10 years. The most important risk factor of recurrent disease is positive/close surgical margins, with a trend for increased risk at the head and neck. The vast majority of recurrences are local and appear during the first few years. No data support adjuvant treatment. The 5-year disease-specific survival is 96%-100%. CONCLUSIONS: cLMS exhibits a moderate risk of local recurrence, low metastatic potential, and excellent disease-specific survival. Surveillance may be focused on physical examination and limited in duration.

item.title: Calendar-defined missed-workday gaps in radiotherapy: a site- and phase-stratified audit with linkage sensitivity analyses.
item.dc:creator: Lei R, Zheng Y, Chen Y, Sun H, Qu A, Jiang P
item.description:
Authors: Lei R, Zheng Y, Chen Y, Sun H, Qu A, Jiang P
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1932765
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42908819



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Missed treatment workdays can prolong overall treatment time and may reduce tumor control, yet routine audits often conflate weekends, statutory holidays, and departmentally accepted rest schedules with untreated institutional workdays. METHODS: We quantified calendar-defined missed-workday gaps-inter-fraction intervals containing ≥1 untreated institutional workday after excluding routine rest days-among patients with first treatment between June 2021 and December 2025 who were linkable between the MOSAIQ radiotherapy information system and the institutional oncology database (1,319 patients; 1,342 episodes). A locked stratified sample of 100 algorithm-positive gaps underwent documentation-based chart review as unplanned relevant (UR) or planned/appropriate (PA). We analyzed linkage sensitivity, opportunity-adjusted site rates with patient-clustered confidence intervals (CIs), opportunity-offset Poisson generalized estimating equations (GEE) including calendar year, and episode-clustered phase GEE. RESULTS: Under the documentation-based chart-review rule, 92 of 100 algorithm-positive gaps were labeled UR (17 department/equipment; 75 patient-factor) and 8 PA. Gaps occurred in 638/1,342 episodes (47.5%; patient-level 48.0%). Linked versus unlinked prevalence was 48.2% versus 51.7% (absolute difference -3.4 percentage points, 95% CI -11.2 to 4.4; P = 0.435). Among subgroups with ≥50 episodes, head and neck had the highest prevalence (75.3%) and breast the lowest (41.3%); opportunity-adjusted rates were 5.63 (cluster-bootstrap 95% CI 4.76-6.52) versus 2.63 (2.36-2.92) per 100 opportunities. Opportunity-offset Poisson GEE with calendar year gave a head-and-neck versus breast incidence rate ratio (IRR) of 2.99 (95% CI 2.18-4.11). An exploratory phase GEE (29,763 intervals; 1,323 clusters) showed a late versus early odds ratio (OR) of 1.31 (95% CI 1.12-1.54; P = 0.0009; absolute rates 2.8% vs 3.6%); after site, year, and intent adjustment, the OR was 1.32 (95% CI 1.12-1.57). CONCLUSIONS: This operational audit of institutional workdays without recorded treatment-rather than clinically confirmed unplanned interruptions-shows frequent gaps after excluding routine rest. Most reviewed positives received patient-factor labels under a documentation rule. Calendar-aware auditing may support departmental monitoring; priority-based compensation remains a proposed application.

item.title: The clinical value of ultrasound radiomics combined with clinical data nomogram in predicting cervical lymph node metastasis of papillary thyroid carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Zhang X, Sun B, Jiang F, Chu Y, Wang X, Sun W, Wei T, Hong R, Ma Q
item.description:
Authors: Zhang X, Sun B, Jiang F, Chu Y, Wang X, Sun W, Wei T, Hong R, Ma Q
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1811434
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42908715



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the predictive value of a nomogram incorporating ultrasound and clinical features for cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in patients with thyroid cancer. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients pathologically diagnosed with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) between April 2024 and January 2025. Radiomics features were extracted from two-dimensional thyroid ultrasound images, and feature selection was performed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO). Five classifiers were compared, and logistic regression was selected to construct the radiomics model. A clinical-radiomics model integrating the radiomics score and clinical predictors, together with a standalone clinical model, was developed using multivariable logistic regression. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated in a held-out internal validation set. RESULTS: Sex, Radscore, age, and thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) levels were identified as independent predictors of CLNM in patients with PTC. Based on these variables, radiomics, clinical, and clinical radiomics models were constructed; the models achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.735, 0.792, and 0.867, respectively, in the validation set. DeLong's test and decision curve analysis (DCA) demonstrated that the clinical radiomics model outperformed the radiomics model in the validation set, offering a higher net clinical benefit. CONCLUSION: A nomogram integrating ultrasound imaging and clinical data effectively predicts the risk of CLNM in patients with PTC and may assist clinicians in developing individualized treatment strategies.

item.title: Construction and validation of a nomogram based on inflammatory, nutritional and metabolic indicators for predicting the risk of papillary thyroid carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Chen Z, Su H, Wu H, Men Q, Lv X, Zhang M, Zhang F
item.description:
Authors: Chen Z, Su H, Wu H, Men Q, Lv X, Zhang M, Zhang F
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1917420
Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the correlation between inflammation, nutrition and metabolic indicators and the risk of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), and to construct and validate a nomogram for predicting PTC risk among patients with thyroid nodules undergoing surgery, to assist clinicians in making more individualized clinical decisions. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective population-based cohort study. METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on the clinical medical records of patients with thyroid masses who underwent surgical treatment at Hebei General Hospital from 2020 to 2024. Independent risk factors for the onset of PTC were screened through Logistic regression analysis. A risk prediction model for the onset of PTC based on inflammatory, nutritional and metabolic indicators was constructed using R4.3.3 software and externally validated. RESULTS: A total of 1727 patients who underwent thyroidectomy for thyroid nodules were enrolled, among whom 1167 patients (67.6%) were pathologically-confirmed papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), and 560 patients (32.4%) had benign thyroid nodules after surgery. Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated combined Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) (OR = 1.887, 95%CI: 1.174-3.031, P = 0.009), combined metabolic syndrome (MetS) (OR = 2.157, 95%CI: 1.449-3.211, P < 0.001), and elevated uric acid (UA) (OR = 1.640, 95%CI: 1.112-2.417, P = 0.013) were independent risk factors for PTC onset. The calibration curve and decision analysis curve also indicate that the nomogram has good predictive performance and clinical application efficacy. CONCLUSION: Combined HT, combined MetS, and elevated UA are independent risk factors for PTC onset, whereas age ≥ 55 years, other marital status, and PNI level represent independent protective factors.

item.dc:creator: Pande N, Moser JC, Chandrasekaran S, Brohl AS, Kulkarni RP, Ma VT
item.description:
Authors: Pande N, Moser JC, Chandrasekaran S, Brohl AS, Kulkarni RP, Ma VT
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18193226
Published: 2026-Oct-07
PMID: 42882919



Abstract:
Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) represents a rare but highly aggressive neuroendocrine skin cancer with limited systemic therapy options for patients who fail or are ineligible for immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Intratumoral (IT) immunotherapy has emerged as a promising strategy, leveraging the accessibility of tumor lesions and their inherent capacity to trigger immune responses, known as abscopal effects. This review synthesizes the current evidence on IT approaches in MCC, including Toll-like receptor agonists, cytokines, and oncolytic viruses, and highlights their distinct mechanisms of action, while emphasizing the critical need for standardized radiographic response assessment of injected and non-injected lesions. Inconsistent documentation of abscopal responses has hindered quantification of IT therapy's systemic potential, particularly in a disease where one-third of patients present with metastases and distant relapse is common. We outline MCC-specific rationale for routine lesion-level tracking, and recommendations for IT trial designs and objectives. Rigorous assessments of abscopal data will clarify IT's role as both rescue therapy and an ICI partner, potentially transforming outcomes in this refractory MCC.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advancement sliding genioplasty effectively corrects convex facial profiles. Characterizing hard and soft tissue changes is critical to optimizing surgical results. Cone-beam computed tomography-based three-dimensional cephalometric analysis is widely adopted to assess craniofacial surgical outcomes. PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to measure the association of hard and soft tissues changes in patients with microgenia undergoing advancement sliding genioplasty. STUDY DESIGN, SAMPLE, AND SETTING: Patients with microgenia were enrolled in this retrospective cohort study from January 2024 to January 2025 at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, The First Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. Those with maxillofacial trauma, secondary jaw deformity, prior chin plasty, or incomplete medical notes were excluded. PREDICTOR VARIABLE: The predictor variable was microgenia severity, dichotomized based on facial convexity angle (FCA): ≤25 ° and >25 °. An FCA > 25 ° indicated more severe deformity. MAIN OUTCOME VARIABLES: The primary outcome variable was soft tissue displacement relative to hard tissue displacement, expressed as the soft-to-hard tissue movement ratio. COVARIATES: Covariates included age, sex, body mass index, mandibular plane angle, and soft tissue thickness. ANALYSES: Descriptive statistics were calculated. Student's t-test or nonparametric tests were used for appropriate group comparisons. Intraclass correlation coefficients assessed intrarater reliability. Spearman's correlation evaluated variable associations. Multivariable linear regression models examined associations between microgenia severity and soft-to-hard tissue movement ratios. A two-tailed P value of < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: The sample comprised 113 subjects with a mean age of 26.7 (4.4); 95 (84.01%) were female. Sagittal soft-to-hard tissue movement ratios ranged from 0.92 (0.13)-0.96 (0.09) to 0.63 (0.11)-0.70 (0.08) for patients with FCA ≤25 °, versus 0.98 (0.12)-1.03 (0.07) to 0.65 (0.07)-0.81 (0.11) in those with FCA>25 °. Intergroup comparison showed a statistically significant sagittal direction difference only at the menton [0.96 (0.09) vs 1.03 (0.07), P < .001]. Multivariable linear regression revealed microgenia severity had no independent association with soft-to-hard tissue movement ratios (all P > .05). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Analysis demonstrated stable soft-to-hard tissue movement ratios in both sagittal and vertical chin movements. The findings provide quantitative evidence facilitating more accurate models for predicting postoperative soft tissue outcomes.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transportability of models for postoperative high-volume cervical nodal disease in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) and the incremental predictive value of molecular variables remain uncertain. Ridge logistic regression (C = 0.1) was selected and applied without refitting. Paired comparisons of 8-variable clinicopathological and 10-variable clinicopathological-molecular models assessed the incremental value of high-risk co-mutation status and mutation count in both cohorts. RESULTS: Internal validation yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.795 (95% CI, 0.745-0.842), average precision (AP) of 0.497 (0.406-0.598), and Brier score of 0.115 (0.098-0.134). External AUROC was 0.752 (0.678-0.821), AP 0.601 (0.498-0.728), and Brier score 0.217 (0.180-0.254). Observed and mean predicted risks were 37.8% and 23.9%, respectively; the observed-to-expected ratio was 1.582 (1.319-1.860) and the weak-calibration slope was 0.831 (0.542-1.191). Net benefit was 0.254 for the model and 0.261 for classifying all patients as high risk (difference, -0.008; 95% CI, -0.051 to 0.033). item.title: Immune-related adverse events are associated with favorable clinical outcomes in esophageal cancer treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Fan J, Chen D, Jia L

Authors: Fan J, Chen D, Jia L
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1948772
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42903106



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are distinctive toxicities associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and have been reported to correlate with clinical outcomes in several cancers. However, whether this association also exists in patients with esophageal cancer (EC) receiving ICIs remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the association between irAEs and clinical outcomes in this population. METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 2, 2026. Eligible studies evaluated the association between irAEs and progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), or disease control rate (DCR). Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled for PFS and OS, whereas odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs were pooled for ORR and DCR using random-effects models. Between-study heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals (PIs), sensitivity analyses, publication bias, prespecified subgroup analyses, and immortal-time bias were also assessed. RESULTS: 14 studies involving 1, 546 patients were included. The occurrence of irAEs was associated with improved PFS (HR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.31-0.63), OS (HR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.46-0.64), ORR (OR, 4.00; 95% CI, 1.58-10.12), and DCR (OR, 3.85; 95% CI, 2.40-6.20). The 95% PIs were 0.16-1.24, 0.44-0.66, 0.19-82.57, and 1.42-10.44 for PFS, OS, ORR, and DCR, respectively, crossing the null value for PFS and ORR. Subgroup estimates were generally similar in direction but remained exploratory. No eligible survival estimates using landmark or time-varying approaches were available for the comparison between patients with and without irAEs. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with EC receiving ICIs, the occurrence of irAEs may be a prognostic marker of favorable outcomes. However, wide PIs for PFS and ORR indicate that these associations may vary across future studies and immortal time bias may overestimate survival associations. This observational evidence derives mainly from East Asian patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and is primarily applicable to these patients. Subgroup findings remain exploratory and require prospective validation. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261346294.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Bleeding is a common concern in dental, oral, and maxillofacial surgery, particularly in patients with increased bleeding risk. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on local and systemic hemostatic agents, including their mechanisms, clinical applications, efficacy, and safety. METHODS: Literature published from January 2020 through November 2025 was reviewed using predefined search terms related to hemostatic agents and surgical bleeding. Clinical studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, guidelines, and consensus statements were considered. Seven clinical cases were also reviewed to demonstrate practical applications of selected hemostatic agents. RESULTS: Mechanical agents provided effective control of routine bleeding, whereas active and flowable agents were useful for persistent or diffuse bleeding. Fibrin-based and combination approaches provided additional support in complex procedures. Tranexamic acid was particularly useful in patients receiving antithrombotic therapy. CONCLUSION: Optimal hemostasis requires a tailored, procedure-specific strategy based on bleeding characteristics, surgical complexity, and patient-specific risk factors.

Abstract:
Patients scheduled for surgery under general anesthesia experience significant stress, including anxiety and fear, partly because of difficulty visualizing the operating room environment; however, preoperative visits to the operating room are often impractical. In oral and maxillofacial surgery, where many patients are young, perioperative anxiety and fear are particularly important issues, yet few studies have evaluated virtual reality (VR)-based operating room visits in this field. item.title: From Molecular Alterations to Risk Prediction: Biomarkers of Actinic Keratosis Progression to Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Meyer T, Stockfleth L, Lang K, Käfferlein HU, Brüning T, Stockfleth E
item.description:
Authors: Meyer T, Stockfleth L, Lang K, Käfferlein HU, Brüning T, Stockfleth E
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18193221
Published: 2026-Oct-06
PMID: 42882915



Abstract:
The high-and in most countries steadily increasing-incidence of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) represents a growing public health challenge. As the majority of cSCCs arise from pre-existing actinic keratosis (AKs), these lesions are recognized as the principal precursors of invasive disease. A comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms driving the progression from AK to cSCC is essential for advancing prevention, facilitating early diagnosis, and enabling targeted therapies. Moreover, this knowledge provides a basis for identifying biomarkers that can predict the risk of malignant transformation. The progression from AK to cSCC is a complex, multistep process driven by the gradual accumulation of genetic, epigenetic, and microenvironmental alterations. Over the past decades, numerous molecular changes associated with this transition have been identified. However, no single biomarker has demonstrated sufficient predictive accuracy for clinical use. This reflects the pronounced molecular heterogeneity of AKs as no individual alteration is uniformly present in all lesions that undergo malignant progression. In addition, numerous proposed biomarkers are also detected in non-progressive AKs and even in non-neoplastic skin, which compromises their sensitivity and specificity for predicting progression to cSCC. Current evidence, therefore, suggests that the most promising strategy for identifying AKs at greatest risk of malignant transformation is the development of a multi-marker panel. This panel, ideally, should integrate molecular signatures encompassing genetic, epigenetic, proliferative, inflammatory, and microenvironmental markers. This review summarizes the molecular factors that currently represent the most promising candidates for inclusion in such a multi-marker panel and discusses their potential clinical utility, while emphasizing the need for validation in well-designed prospective longitudinal studies.

item.title: Endoscopic Endonasal Approaches to Anterior Cranial Base Meningiomas: Indications, Limitations, and Surgical Decision-Making.
item.dc:creator: Chopra M, John D, Cote DJ, Zada G
item.description:
Authors: Chopra M, John D, Cote DJ, Zada G
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18193217
Published: 2026-Oct-06
PMID: 42882911



Abstract:
Endoscopic endonasal surgery (EES) has fundamentally changed the management of anterior skull base meningiomas by enabling access to many lesions through a direct minimally invasive corridor that avoids traditional transcranial exposure. Improvements in endoscopic optical technology, surgical instrumentation, and skull base reconstruction have steadily expanded the range of tumors that can be treated through an endonasal approach. Even so, EES is not appropriate for every lesion, making thoughtful patient selection and surgical team experience the most important determinants of surgical success. This review explores where EES fits in the contemporary management of anterior skull base meningiomas, including olfactory groove, tuberculum sellae, and planum sphenoidale meningiomas, with particular attention to its indications, limitations, and situations in which EES may not be appropriate. Evidence comparing endoscopic endonasal and transcranial approaches for anterior skull base meningiomas is reviewed, with attention to how tumor anatomy, oncologic objectives, and individual patient characteristics influence the choice of approach. A major consideration is how surgical morbidity can be minimized without compromising oncologic and safety outcomes. Current strategies to protect critical neurovascular structures, reduce the risk of cerebrospinal fluid leakage, and improve skull base durability, including advances in vascularized reconstruction techniques, are discussed. Emerging outcome data and the evolving learning curve associated with EES are also reviewed. Rather than presenting EES as a universal solution, the evidence points toward a patient-centered approach in which operative strategy and clinical decision making is guided by tumor characteristics, anatomy, and surgical goals.

item.title: PET Tumour Segmentation in Head and Neck Cancer: Reproducibility, Reader Dependence and Concordance with CT-Defined Tumour Volume in a 154-Patient Cohort.
item.dc:creator: Pirson AS, Delahaut G, Georis R, Deheneffe S, Van der Vorst S, Kudura K
item.description:
Authors: Pirson AS, Delahaut G, Georis R, Deheneffe S, Van der Vorst S, Kudura K
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18193214
Published: 2026-Oct-05
PMID: 42882908



Abstract:
Purpose: Volumetric PET biomarkers carry substantial prognostic value in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), yet their clinical implementation is hampered by segmentation heterogeneity. A fundamental and unresolved question is which segmentation method is most suitable for routine clinical use, both for a reader experienced in PET segmentation and for a reader without PET segmentation experience, such as an ENT surgeon or a radiation oncologist. This study addressed this question by assessing the intra- and interobserver reproducibility of four PET segmentation methods in MIM Maestro Software Version 7.4.2, identifying tumour-related determinants of variability, and examining concordance between PET-derived metabolic tumour volume (MTV) and CT-based gross tumour volume (GTV). Methods: Two readers with contrasting PET segmentation experience, a nuclear medicine physician experienced in PET segmentation (R1) and an ENT surgeon without prior PET segmentation training (R2), applied four methods to the primary tumours of 154 patients with HNSCC (oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx or larynx) treated with definitive (chemo)radiotherapy between 2010 and 2021: fixed absolute thresholds at SUV 3.0 and 4.0, a relative threshold at 41% of the maximum standardised uptake value (SUVmax), and a gradient edge-detection algorithm (PET Edge+). R1 segmented twice with a washout of at least 4 weeks; R2 performed one session and delineated CT-GTV in the 85 patients whose PET/CT-derived CT served directly as the radiotherapy planning scan. The second session of R1 served as the reference for all interobserver and MTV-GTV analyses. Agreement was assessed by ICC (two-way mixed model), coefficient of variation, repeatability coefficient and Bland-Altman analysis; determinants of variability by a multivariable linear mixed-effects model with a random intercept per patient. Results: All four methods demonstrated excellent intraobserver (ICC 0.993 to >0.999) and interobserver (ICC 0.989-0.996) reproducibility. SUV3.0 generated significantly more relative error than SUV41% (β = +3.1%; 95% CI 0.89, 5.3). PET Edge+ was the only method for which a significant method × reader interaction was observed in this reader pair: the reader without PET segmentation experience generated more error than the reader experienced in PET segmentation (β = +7.1%; 95% CI 3.9, 10), an effect concentrated in smaller tumours (below approximately 15 mL); in the 85-patient GTV subset, where tumours were larger on average, the interobserver ICC for PET Edge+ was 0.997. GTV concordance was good for three of four methods (ICC 0.808-0.895); SUV41% showed only moderate concordance (ICC 0.572). Conclusions: All four methods provided excellent volumetric reproducibility within a single clinical software platform, but they differed in reader dependence and in agreement with CT-defined GTV. Rather than supporting a universal segmentation standard, these findings suggest that the method should be selected according to its intended application, pending multicentre confirmation.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate (a) changes in caries experience, (b) changes in periodontal status, and (c) the need for dental extractions in a cohort of patients treated with radiotherapy (RT) and chemoradiotherapy (RTCT) for head and neck cancer (HNC). METHODS: This prospective cohort study was approved by the local Ethics Committee (Ref. 22858/18) and registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT04009161). The study population consisted of patients with HNC who, prior to RT, underwent a dental examination followed by the elimination of oral foci of infection and were then enrolled in a follow-up program. Oral cavity RT dose was obtained contouring the 'buccal mucosa' organ at risk (OAR). RESULTS: In total, 113 patients were included (median follow-up: 44.77 months). The sample mainly included oral, oropharyngeal, nasopharyngeal and laryngeal cancers (89/113, 78.8%). Salivary glands, hypopharynx and other sites accounted for a minority of the cases (24/113, 21.2%). Seventeen patients (34.7%) experienced worsening of oral health status over time, which was associated with smoking (OR = 4.7, 95% CI: 1.27-17.37; p = 0.02). item.title: Cutaneous Neoplasms with Sebaceous Differentiation: A Comprehensive Update on Clinical, Histopathological and Molecular Classification.
item.dc:creator: Wiedemeyer K, Ferreira I, Adams DJ, Brenn T
item.description:
Authors: Wiedemeyer K, Ferreira I, Adams DJ, Brenn T
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18193209
Published: 2026-Oct-04
PMID: 42882904



Abstract:
Cutaneous sebaceous neoplasms are rare adnexal tumours differentiated towards sebaceous glands, spanning a biological spectrum from benign (sebaceous adenoma, sebaceoma, nevus sebaceus) to outright malignant (sebaceous carcinoma). Most tumours are sporadic and solitary, with a predilection for the head and neck of elderly adults, but a clinically important subset is observed in the setting of Lynch syndrome/Muir-Torre syndrome. Recent large-scale genomic and transcriptomic studies have provided insights into the pathogenesis of these unique neoplasms, revealing a genetically heterogeneous landscape shaped by mismatch repair deficiency, UV damage, and abnormalities in several other key signalling pathways. The inclusion of nevus sebaceus within the sebaceous tumour family in the WHO 5th Edition of Skin Tumours reflects a conceptual shift, recognising nevus sebaceus as a clonal, mutation-driven neoplasm and a precursor lesion for secondary tumour development.

item.title: Comparative Evaluation of Feature Selection Algorithms for Predicting Radiation-Induced Complications in Head and Neck Cancer Using Multimodal CT and MRI Radiomics.
item.dc:creator: Khajetash B, Deevband MR, Stokes WA, Tavakoli M
item.description:
Authors: Khajetash B, Deevband MR, Stokes WA, Tavakoli M
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18193200
Published: 2026-Oct-03
PMID: 42882894



Abstract:
Head and neck cancer (HNC) presents a significant challenge due to its anatomic complexity and treatment-related complications such as sticky saliva and xerostomia, which critically impair patients' quality of life. Recent advancements in imaging technologies, using the concept of radiomics, offer promising approaches for predicting these complications and ultimately reducing their incidence. In this regard, robust feature selection is critical in radiomics-based predictive modeling due to the high dimensionality, redundancy, and instability of extracted imaging biomarkers. This study aims to evaluate nine distinct feature selection algorithms-Boruta, Kruskal, Recursive Maximum Relevance minimum redundancy (R-MRmr), Relief, Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), Forward Selection (FS), Backward Elimination (BE), Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), and Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-as a feature-transformation comparator for predicting sticky saliva and xerostomia in HNC patients using clinical, dosimetric, MRI and CT radiomics data. The study involved 250 HNC patients who underwent radiotherapy from three different institutions. From MRI and CT images, a total of 321 radiomic features (107 from each CT, T1, and T2-weighted MRI) along with 20 clinical and dosimetric features were extracted. The predictive robustness of feature selection methods was further evaluated across five machine-learning classifiers, including K-nearest neighbors (KNN), support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), logistic regression (LR), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), were initially benchmarked using a common feature selection procedure, after which SVM was selected as the reference classifier for systematic comparison of the feature-reduction approaches. Model performance was assessed using metrics objectives such as Area Under the Curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. Among the evaluated feature selection approaches, R-MRmr and Relief generally yielded better discrimination, although performance varied according to toxicity endpoint and imaging modality. The highest AUCs were 0.85 for early sticky saliva (R-MRmr, T1-weighted MRI), 0.96 for early xerostomia (R-MRmr, T1-weighted MRI), 0.65 for late sticky saliva (Relief, combined CT+T1+T2), and 0.88 for late xerostomia (Relief, T1-weighted MRI). T1-weighted MRI frequently provided better individual-modality performance, whereas combining all three imaging modalities did not consistently improve discrimination. These findings demonstrate that the choice of feature selection strategy and imaging modality can materially influence radiomics-based toxicity prediction.

item.title: Chk1/2 Inhibition by AZD7762 Enhances Andrographolide-Induced DNA Damage, Impairs DNA Repair, and Promotes Apoptosis in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma CAL-33 Cells.

item.description:

Abstract:
Background: Andrographolide (AG), a diterpenoid lactone and a major constituent of Andrographis paniculata, has shown promising antiproliferative effect on diverse cancer cell lines, including head and neck cancer. However, a significant anti-proliferative effect is observed only at high micromolar concentrations. Further, AG has been shown to have poor oral bioavailability. Therefore, it is essential to consider mechanism-based combinations that could synergistically enhance the therapeutic potential of this compound so that efficacy can be achieved in concentrations that are systemically achievable. Objective: The present study is aimed to evaluate the anticancer effects and associated molecular alterations of an AG and Chk1/2 inhibitor combination in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (CAL-33) cells since the earlier studies have suggested ATM/ATR/Chk1/2-mediated activation of DNA damage checkpoints. Methods: Normal FHs74int cells and HNSCC cells (CAL-33 and FaDu) were used to assess cell proliferation and cell death. Cell cycle distribution and apoptosis were analyzed by flow cytometry and Acridine orange/EtBr, respectively, in CAL-33 cells. DNA damage in CAL-33 and FaDu cells was assessed by comet assay. Changes in the expression of proteins implicated in apoptosis, cell cycle progression, and DNA damage signaling were examined using Western blotting. Results: While AG did not show any significant changes in the growth or cell death of normal FHs74int cells, it strongly inhibited proliferation of HNSCC cells, concomitant with G2/M arrest and apoptosis. AG and AZD7762 showed an IC50 of 2.743 μM and 0.02600 μM, respectively, on cell proliferation in CAL-33 cells. Furthermore, AG caused an accumulation of intracellular ROS, which was inhibited by treatment with N-acetylcysteine. Chk1, Chk2 and γH2AX phosphorylation were induced in a dose-dependent manner by treatment with AG. The combination of AG with Chk1/2 inhibitor AZD7762 showed a synergistic effect in inhibiting cell proliferation with a CI of 0.4 through inhibition of DNA repair and premature mitotic entry, ultimately resulting in programmed cell death. Conclusions: These findings provide evidence that AG selectively targets DNA damage and repair in HNSCC CAL-33 cells via cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. Further, the anticancer potential of AG can be significantly enhanced by combination with the Chk1/2 inhibitor AZD7762, preventing repair of AG-induced DNA damage and amplifying checkpoint stress responses, resulting in enhanced apoptotic cell death. Together, these findings support the therapeutic potential of AG and highlight checkpoint kinase inhibition as a rational combination strategy for HNSCC treatment.

item.title: Second Primary Malignancies in Gastrointestinal Cancer Survivors: Epidemiology, Risk Factors, and Future Prediction Models.
item.dc:creator: Yadav J, Balizzakiwa T, Goyal H
item.description:
Authors: Yadav J, Balizzakiwa T, Goyal H
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18193195
Published: 2026-Oct-03
PMID: 42882890



Abstract:
Advances in gastrointestinal (GI) cancer care have produced a growing population of long-term survivors at risk of second primary malignancies (SPMs). SPM definitions vary across studies, and SPMs remain underrepresented in cancer forecasting and prediction tools for GI cancer survivors. We conducted a narrative review across major GI cancer subtypes, summarizing site-specific SPM risk, key etiological pathways, and available prediction tools. Approximately one in ten colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors develops an SPM at ten years (pooled SIR ~1.15), a figure specific to CRC that does not generalize to other GI sites. Gastric cancer survivors carry excess risk of thyroid (O/E 2.00), esophageal, small intestinal, and pancreatic (O/E 1.60) malignancy, amplified by radiotherapy. Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma survivors show markedly elevated risk of upper aerodigestive tract tumors, consistent with field cancerization. Lynch syndrome (~16% second CRC risk at 10 years) and familial adenomatous polyposis (near-100% lifetime CRC risk without colectomy) confer some of the highest lifetime risks of metachronous GI malignancy reported to date. Most forecasting frameworks treat cancer incidence as a single event and do not adequately capture survivor-specific transitions, competing mortality, or germline susceptibility. GI cancer survivors form a distinct group whose risk is often overlooked. Harmonizing SPM definitions, extending multistate and competing-risk modeling, and integrating hereditary-risk stratification are near-term priorities for individualized surveillance.

item.title: Expression of Mitophagy-Associated Factors and Their Associations with Metastasis and Prognosis in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Matsuzoe Y, Takeda D, Saito I, Murakami Y, Murakami A, Tadokoro Y, Hirota J, Kakei Y, Akashi M, Hasegawa T
item.description:
Authors: Matsuzoe Y, Takeda D, Saito I, Murakami Y, Murakami A, Tadokoro Y, Hirota J, Kakei Y, Akashi M, Hasegawa T
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18193194
Published: 2026-Oct-03
PMID: 42882888



Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Mitophagy-associated factors have been implicated in tumor behavior and patient outcomes; however, their clinical significance depends on tumor type, stage, and microenvironmental context, and consistent conclusions remain lacking. We aimed to comprehensively assess the expression of mitophagy-associated factors in a moderate-sized cohort of patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and clarify their prognostic significance. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study included 197 patients with OSCC who underwent primary surgical resection between August 2013 and October 2018. Immunohistochemical expression of mitophagy-associated factors, including transcription factor EB (TFEB), nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2), activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4), Parkin, PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1), and mitochondrial ubiquitin ligase (MITOL), was evaluated. Associations between protein expression and clinicopathological parameters, local control, 5-year disease-specific survival (DSS), regional control, and distant metastasis were analyzed. RESULTS: High expression of NRF2 and TFEB was significantly related with decreased DSS, poor regional control, and increased distant metastasis. High ATF4 expression was associated with distant metastasis and showed no association with DSS. Parkin, PINK1, and MITOL showed no significant association with patient outcomes. Explanatory multivariable analysis showed associations between high TFEB expression, vascular invasion, extranodal extension, and disease-specific mortality. CONCLUSIONS: TFEB expression showed an exploratory association with aggressive tumor behavior and poor prognosis in OSCC, warranting further investigation. However, because immunohistochemical evaluation measures protein expression rather than mitophagy flux or mitochondrial turnover, these findings represent associations between mitophagy-associated factor expression and clinical outcomes and do not directly demonstrate altered mitophagy activity.

item.title: Self-management support interventions for patients with cancer treatment-related oral mucositis: a scoping review.
item.dc:creator: Yan H, Liu X, Li J, Ma D, Wang W, Xie Y, Wang L, Ning L
item.description:
Authors: Yan H, Liu X, Li J, Ma D, Wang W, Xie Y, Wang L, Ning L
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1950737
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42891185



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cancer treatment-related oral mucositis (OM) is one of the most common adverse effects of cancer treatment and can substantially impair patients' quality of life. Its effective management depends heavily on patients' continuous self-management. This scoping review aimed to systematically map the intervention components, delivery modes, and existing limitations of self-management support interventions, thereby providing evidence to inform the optimization of intervention strategies. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews. Seven databases, including PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CINAHL, Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and WanFang, were searched from inception to May 10, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Data were charted using a standardized form and summarized using descriptive numerical and content analyses. RESULTS: A total of 7,132 records were identified, and 16 studies were ultimately included, comprising 9 quasi-experimental studies, 6 randomized controlled trials, and 1 mixed-methods study. The interventions were primarily hospital-based and nurse-led, with some incorporating digital tools or written materials. Reported outcomes generally included OM-related clinical outcomes, quality of life, self-management-related outcomes, and nutritional status, although the direction and magnitude of findings varied across studies. CONCLUSIONS: Existing studies have reported potential improvements in OM-related and self-management-related outcomes following self-management support interventions. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of heterogeneity in study designs, intervention components, and outcome measures, together with the absence of critical appraisal. Further well-designed studies using standardized outcome measures are needed to strengthen the evidence base.

item.title: Pretreatment body mass index as a prognostic factor for clinical course and survival in primary surgically treated oral squamous cell carcinoma - a retrospective study.
item.dc:creator: Floegel E, Brandenburg LS, Arias Romero JA, Vach K, Metzger MC, Schmelzeisen R, Wüster J
item.description:
Authors: Floegel E, Brandenburg LS, Arias Romero JA, Vach K, Metzger MC, Schmelzeisen R, Wüster J
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1894543
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42890580



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), body mass index (BMI) is an available but imperfect marker of nutritional reserve. Evidence on pretreatment BMI in surgery-based European OSCC cohorts remains limited, especially regarding perioperative outcomes. This study evaluated associations of pretreatment BMI with overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS), and perioperative outcomes after curative-intent R0 resection. METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included adult patients with previously untreated primary OSCC, available pretreatment BMI, and curative-intent R0 surgery between 2014 and 2023. BMI was assessed continuously and by World Health Organization (WHO) categories. OS and RFS were analyzed using multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, pathological T category, nodal status, microvascular free-flap reconstruction, and diabetes mellitus. Perioperative outcomes included red blood cell (RBC) transfusion, RBC units transfused, percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) placement, and intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay. RESULTS: A total of 274 patients with available pretreatment BMI were included; 116 deaths occurred. Five-year OS ranged from 31.4% in patients classified as underweight to 82.0% in patients with obesity. Higher BMI was associated with lower mortality (HR per 1 kg/m² 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99; p = 0.013), and obesity was associated with improved OS compared with normal weight (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.26-0.96; p = 0.037). BMI was not significantly associated with RFS after adjustment (HR per 1 kg/m² 0.97, 95% CI 0.93-1.00; p = 0.080). Higher BMI was associated with fewer perioperative RBC transfusions (any transfusion: OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.98; p = 0.012; number of units: OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.82-0.95; p = 0.001). BMI was not independently associated with PEG placement or hospital length of stay; ICU findings depended on BMI modeling. DISCUSSION: Higher pretreatment BMI was associated with better OS and lower perioperative RBC transfusion requirements, whereas associations with RFS and most other perioperative outcomes were not significant after adjustment. Given the retrospective design and limitations of BMI as a body-composition marker, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Pretreatment BMI may help identify low-BMI patients warranting early supportive-care assessment.

item.title: Integrated genome-wide DNA methylation and transcriptomic analysis prioritizes EPHA5 as a candidate non-invasive epigenetic biomarker for oral squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Demokan S, Özemek B, Turna S, Cömert S, Şen C, Avcı K, Özkan A, Şen S, Poda M, Ulusan M, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Demokan S, Özemek B, Turna S, Cömert S, Şen C, Avcı K, Özkan A, Şen S, Poda M, Ulusan M, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1932336
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42890571



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains a major clinical challenge because of delayed diagnosis and the lack of validated non-invasive biomarkers for OSCC detection. Epigenetic alterations during oral carcinogenesis represent promising biomarker candidates. This study aimed to prioritize clinically relevant epigenetic biomarkers and validate EPHA5 using an integrated genome-wide DNA methylation and transcriptomic approach. EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: Genome-wide DNA methylation and transcriptomic profiling were performed to identify epigenetically deregulated genes in OSCC. Candidate genes were prioritized by integrating DNA methylation, transcriptomic data and biological relevance. EPHA5 was subsequently selected for validation and evaluated by quantitative methylation-specific PCR (QMSP) and quantitative real-time PCR (QRT-PCR) in tissue, saliva and serum samples from independent cohorts comprising patients with OSCC, oral premalignant lesions (OPML) and healthy controls. RESULTS: Genome-wide analysis identified 661 upregulated and 577 downregulated genes together with 2,431 differentially methylated regions corresponding to 1,776 genes. Integrated analysis generated a panel of 51 candidate genes, from which EPHA5 was prioritized using integrated DNA methylation, gene expression, pathway enrichment and biological relevance. EPHA5 promoter hypermethylation was detected in 66.7% of OSCC tumors, whereas concurrent promoter hypermethylation and reduced expression were observed in 28.6% of tumors. Methylation was also detected in 54.5% of OPML lesions and in the saliva of 47.6% of OSCC patients but was rarely detected in healthy controls. Tumor EPHA5 methylation significantly discriminated OSCC from healthy controls (AUC = 0.780, p = 0.004; sensitivity, 71.4%; specificity, 75%). Salivary EPHA5 methylation also significantly discriminated OSCC from healthy controls (AUC = 0.717, p = 0.025; sensitivity, 52.4%; specificity, 87.5%), whereas serum methylation showed no significant diagnostic utility (AUC = 0.571, p = 0.462). Discrimination between OSCC and OPML was limited and did not reach statistical significance (tumor AUC = 0.662, p = 0.068; salivary AUC = 0.600, p = 0.264). CONCLUSIONS: Frequent tumor hypermethylation together with detectable salivary methylation supports further evaluation of EPHA5 as a candidate non-invasive epigenetic biomarker for OSCC. However, its moderate diagnostic performance, limited discrimination between OSCC and OPML, and lack of external validation indicate that larger prospective studies and evaluation within multimarker methylation panels are required before clinical implementation.

item.title: Same-Day Coordination of Mohs Surgery, Lymphoscintigraphy, and Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy for Merkel Cell Carcinoma: A Single-Center Feasibility Report.
item.dc:creator: Ruesch VH, Thrush J, Bena JF, Ricotti C, Piliang M, McEnery-Stonelake M, Michalski-McNeely BM, Meine J, Lucas J, Poblete-Lopez C, et al.

Authors: Ruesch VH, Thrush J, Bena JF, Ricotti C, Piliang M, McEnery-Stonelake M, Michalski-McNeely BM, Meine J, Lucas J, Poblete-Lopez C, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18193187
Published: 2026-Oct-02
PMID: 42882880



Abstract:
Background/Objectives: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is an aggressive neuroendocrine tumor, most commonly occurring on the head and neck. Incidence of MCC is rising with the aging population. Five-year overall survival (OS) for localized MCC is 50.6%; 5-year OS for patients with distant metastases is 13.5%. The purpose of this study is to determine if coordination of care for the treatment of MCC is logistically feasible, and provide a description of the patient population observed at this institution. Methods: All patients with MCC diagnosis from January 2012-June 2024 were identified at our tertiary care center. All patients with MCC were added to our non-melanoma skin cancer registry. Outcomes were compared between those treated with our "Merkel cell carcinoma in a day" (MIAD) protocol and those receiving the standard treatment protocol. Results: No significant differences were detected in the recurrence rate, transit metastasis, distant metastasis, and disease-specific death. Nodal metastasis was higher in the MIAD group (HR 4.94, 95% CI 1.08-22.6, p = 0.039, six events total). Both groups had similar times to treatment and treatment within 30 days of diagnosis. Conclusions: MCC is a rare and aggressive tumor, often exhibiting subclinical tumor spread. Mohs micrographic surgery ensures 100% peripheral and deep margin assessment, with potential for tissue sparing. With thoughtful coordination, lymphoscintigraphy can be completed on the same day as Mohs surgery followed by sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) and reconstructive surgery.

item.title: Nasopharyngeal Angiofibroma in Adults: Age-Stratified Stage Distribution, Clinical Outcomes, and Exploratory Tumor-Normal Genomics.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (NA) is generally benign, but recurrent disease and rare malignant transformation remain clinically relevant beyond adolescence. We examined adult clinical presentations, records of malignant transformation, and age-related differences in stage distribution. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 289 surgically treated patients from January 2006 through June 2026. Radkowski stage distributions were compared between patients aged > 30 and ≤30 years using exact tests. Detailed clinical records were reviewed for 16 adults, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) annotation summaries were examined for one tumor-blood pair. RESULTS: Twenty-five patients (8.7%) were older than 30 years; stage was available for 287 patients. In the detailed adult subgroup, a prior pathology-slide record described focal malignant transformation with a Ki-67 index of approximately 50% in one recurrent tumor. Two other patients had database transformation entries without accompanying pathological documentation. Four recurrences and three deaths were recorded, all in stage IIIB disease. Three men had colorectal or rectal cancer histories. Low-, intermediate-, and advanced-stage tumors accounted for 36.0%, 36.0%, and 28.0% of adult cases, compared with 17.6%, 57.3%, and 25.2% of younger cases (p = 0.0493). The genomic annotations showed a C>A-predominant substitution spectrum. CONCLUSIONS: Adult NA included recurrent stage IIIB disease and a documented record of focal malignant transformation. Stage distributions differed between age groups. These clinical observations support pathological reassessment of recurrent tumors. The single-case genomic findings remain descriptive annotations.

item.title: Cobimetinib + Vemurafenib in Patients With BRAF V600E-Mutant Papillary Thyroid and Biliary Tract Cancers: Results From the TAPUR Study.

item.description:

Published: 2026-Oct-01
